hypotheses.description: email-service is accumulating an internal backlog under sustained checkout traffic, causing queue depth and processing latency to grow until some confirmation requests time out or fail.
email-service has a resource leak or saturation issue (for example, connection/thread pool exhaustion or memory growth) that worsens over time under load, slowing email processing progressively.
checkout-service may be generating bursts of duplicate or retrying confirmation requests during sustained traffic, increasing load on email-service and causing delayed or failed email processing.

tool_history.reasoning: The unresolved question is whether email-service is slowing because it is internally backing up/saturating or because it is leaking resources, versus being overloaded by duplicate/retrying requests from checkout. We already have metrics showing rising RSS and worsening p95 latency, which suggests a service-side degradation but does not reveal the mechanism. Application logs from email-service are the next best discriminator: they can show queue buildup, worker timeouts, connection/thread pool exhaustion, retry storms, GC or OOM warnings, and per-request failures that would support backlog/saturation or resource-leak hypotheses. They may also reveal whether the service is receiving repeated duplicate confirmation requests rather than single steady traffic.

The unresolved question is whether the email-service degradation is purely internal (backlog/resource leak) or being driven by the upstream checkout-service sending duplicate/retrying confirmation requests. We already have email-service metrics and logs showing rising RSS and worsening email latency, which support service-side degradation but do not explain the trigger. The most useful next evidence is checkout-service metrics, especially request/retry/error rates and any spike patterns that could indicate duplicate confirmation submissions or retry storms under sustained traffic. This would directly test the third hypothesis and help distinguish upstream load amplification from an isolated email-service issue.

result.root_cause: email-service progressively degraded under sustained checkout traffic due to internal resource saturation/backlog growth, with memory usage rising sharply and email processing latency increasing until confirmation email processing began failing.
result.explanation: The investigation showed a clear time-correlated degradation within email-service. RSS increased from 128 MiB to 782 MiB over the incident window, while p95 email processing latency reached 1840 ms. Logs moved from successful processing to elevated latency, then memory pressure warnings, and finally a processing failure after a memory allocation error. This supports the hypotheses that email-service was building an internal backlog and/or hitting a resource saturation condition under sustained load. The evidence does not establish a checkout-side retry/duplicate burst, so that remains an open possibility but not the primary cause.
